content.title: About
content.content: Boiled peanuts are shelled peanuts that have been cooked in salted water until tender. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a soft‑crunchy texture. Boiled peanuts are enjoyed as a snack and are also used in salads, Asian dishes, and confectionery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts.
Boiled peanuts are a popular street‑food snack in the southern United States and parts of Asia.
They are botanically related to soybeans, beans, and peas.
Often they are boiled with aromatic spices such as garlic, paprika, and cumin.
Boiled peanuts can be processed into peanut butter, paste, and flour.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanuts provide about 25 % protein, making them a good plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in peanuts is monounsaturated, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Contains magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle, nerve, and bone function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in peanuts aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common allergens and can cause severe reactions.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Peanuts are calorie‑dense, so portion size should be moderated.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking before boiling lowers its level.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Boiled peanuts are often salted; people with hypertension should choose unsalted versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled peanuts can be eaten straight from the shell as a snack, added to salads, rice or noodle dishes, or used in sauces and spreads. They can also be ground into flour for baking or turned into homemade peanut butter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled peanuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them refrigerated, where they stay fresh for 2–3 weeks. Discard any nuts that show mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
